description: Is a decision-support tool using NASA SMAP and POWER data to optimize crop rotations for soil health and water conservation. We are modeling contrasting climates—from Madison, WI (corn, soy, winter cover crops) to Costa Rica (corn, beans, tropical rotation)—to help farmers adapt to extreme weather. Looking for teammates interested in data analysis, agriculture, or UI/UX design to build a functional, data-driven prototype!
summary: RealAgroData is an interactive, bilingual decision-support web application designed to help farmers and agronomists adapt crop rotation strategies to changing climate conditions using real-time NASA satellite and meteorological data.   Addressing the Field Shift challenge, our platform integrates a live connection to the NASA POWER API to fetch 5-year daily precipitation, temperature, humidity, and evapotranspiration datasets for any global coordinates. By combining these live climate metrics with baseline soil texture data (SoilGrids), 36-month vegetation indices (Sentinel-2 NDVI), and historical crop sequences (CropScape CDL), the application evaluates and compares conventional, water-conserving, and regenerative rotation scenarios.   Through clear visual risk matrices, bare-soil alerts, and an interactive financial ROI calculator, RealAgroData bridges the gap between complex Earth observation datasets and actionable, sustainable farm management decisions—protecting soil health, optimizing water resilience, and safeguarding agricultural yields.
details:
What It Does & How It Works RealAgroData is an interactive, bilingual (English/Spanish) agronomic decision-support web application built for the Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge. Users select regional presets (such as Madison, Wisconsin or Guanacaste, Costa Rica) or enter custom global coordinates. The app connects live via REST API to NASA POWER (power.larc.nasa.gov) to download 1,826 days (5 years) of daily precipitation, surface temperature, relative humidity, and evapotranspiration data. It cross-references these live climate series with baseline soil texture data (SoilGrids), 36-month vegetation phenology (Sentinel-2 NDVI), and 3-year historical crop sequences (CropScape CDL) to evaluate and compare three rotation pathways: Conventional, Water-Conserving, and Regenerative.

Benefits & Intended Impact By translating raw Earth observation datasets into actionable field decisions, RealAgroData helps farmers and agronomists mitigate drought, frost, and extreme heat risks, prevent soil erosion through bare-soil alerts, and improve long-term organic carbon retention. Its built-in financial ROI calculator empowers producers to evaluate yield stability and input cost savings before committing to a multi-year rotation shift.

Tools, Languages & Architecture

  • Frontend & Visualization: HTML5, JavaScript (ES6+), React, Recharts (for interactive evapotranspiration/precipitation charts and 36-month NDVI heatmaps), and Tailwind CSS with automatic dark/light mode support.
  • Data Integration: Live client-side fetch() integration with the NASA POWER API, paired with custom CSV upload capabilities for farm-specific records.
  • Hosting & Deployment: Publicly hosted as a zero-backend single-page application via GitHub Pages ([https://meliazumbado-collab.github.io/realagrodata/](https://meliazumbado-collab.github.io/realagrodata/)).

Creativity & Design Factors Considered

  • Dual-Audience UX: We designed a seamless toggle between a simplified "Farmer Hero" view (traffic-light decision badges, plain-language alerts, and clear financial impact) and a Technical/Agronomist view (full meteorological risk matrices, methodology, and NASA data provenance).
  • Accessibility & Field Readiness: Built as a lightweight, self-contained web app that runs smoothly on any browser without expensive hardware, supporting bilingual accessibility and local CSV overrides when field connectivity is limited.
